## What's new
- **Accept self-signed certificates** – if Radarr, Sonarr, qBittorrent, NZBGet or Seerr runs on `https://` with a self-signed or locally signed certificate (e.g. your own CA), tick **Accept self-signed certificate** for that service in **⚙ Settings**
  - certificate verification is skipped **only for that service's address** – every other connection (other services, the GitHub update check) still verifies certificates
  - *Test connection* follows the checkbox in the form, so you can try it before saving
  - also available as `RADARR_INSECURE`, `SONARR_INSECURE`, `NZBGET_INSECURE`, `QBIT_INSECURE`, `SEERR_INSECURE` (`true`/`false`)
- **Clearer certificate errors** – a self-signed certificate now says which option to enable; expired certificates and certificates that don't match the address get their own messages

## Fixes
- Checkboxes in Settings now fall back to their own default when a value has never been saved

## Upgrade

**Docker**
```bash
docker pull ghcr.io/moordrak/arrhub:1.8.0   # or :latest
docker compose up -d                          # if you use docker-compose.yml
```

**Proxmox LXC** (on the Proxmox host)
```bash
pct exec <CTID> -- bash -c "$(curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/moordrak/arrhub/main/install.sh)"
```

**Debian / Ubuntu**
```bash
bash -c "$(curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/moordrak/arrhub/main/install.sh)"
```

Your existing `config.json` is kept; the option is off for every service until you enable it.

**Full changelog:** https://github.com/moordrak/arrhub/compare/v1.7.0...v1.8.0
